title: Zone fallback criteria, leadership contracts, and DR runbook
content:
Context and intent:

This note collects practical, operational guidance intended for the platform team and on-call SREs about *when* to run active-active control plane, when to prefer active-passive, what the leadership contract must guarantee, and a concise DR/evacuation runbook for cross-region events. This is deliberately pragmatic: tradeoffs, acceptance criteria, and run actions rather than long theoretical treatments.

Audience: platform eng, on-call SREs, release owners for control-plane changes.

High-level decision summary (1-line):
- Use active-active for low-latency cross-region control plane needs when read-dominant operations and automated conflict resolution are possible; prefer active-passive when write-safety, small blast radius, and deterministic failovers are higher priority.

Key dimensions we weigh:
- Consistency surface: control-plane writes (routing rules, customer config) vs reads (status, metrics).
- Blast radius: how many customers/regions impacted by split-brain or stale leader view.
- Convergence time: how quickly state can be reconciled without manual intervention.
- Operator complexity: automation, debugging, and rehearsal costs.
- Latency impact: both steady-state control operations and failover latency.

Decision matrix (short checklist):
1) If >40% of write operations are low-frequency config updates and safety requires single-writer semantics -> Active-passive.
2) If control-plane is predominantly read-heavy (health/metrics, non-authoritative caches) and writes can be versioned/merged -> Active-active is acceptable.
3) If customers require sub-200ms control-plane API Across regions -> Active-active with local leader proxies.
4) If regional independence during network partitions is critical -> prefer active-passive with pre-authorized failover windows.

Leadership contract (what a leader must guarantee):
- Exclusive authoritative write acceptance for leader-scoped keys.
- Lease-based leadership with clear TTL and renewals (lease TTL <= 10s for low-latency failover; configurable per environment).
- Observable metrics: lease_acquired, lease_renew_failed, leadership_transitions, leader_epoch (monotonic).
- Idempotent apply semantics for control writes and a monotonically-increasing revision token returned to clients.
- Non-leader behavior: read-only proxy plus redirect header providing current leader id.

Leader election patterns evaluated (practical notes):
- Consensus (RAFT-like): robust, simple to reason about, deterministic. Suitable for active-passive and single-cluster leader election across regions using arbiter nodes. Drawback: cross-region consensus cost unless lightweight quorum design is used.
- Lease + fencing tokens: cheap and simple; beware clock skew and delayed fencing on network partitions. Use in conjunction with monotonic revision tokens.
- External arbiter service (small fleet in multiple regions): reduces cross-region quorum cost but adds an external dependency to manage.

Suggested hybrid pattern (what we've landed on for most cases):
- Per-region local leader + global arbiter for final arbitration.
- Lease TTL short (8s) with heartbeats; on lease loss local node enters read-only mode immediately.
- Global arbiter (3 instances across 3 regions) used only when local region experiences network partition affecting quorum.

Routing policy primitives to implement (examples):
- route.by_region_preference([primary, fallback1, fallback2]) -> prefer local control-plane leader for config updates unless unavailable for > 2 * lease_TTL.
- route.by_customer_tier(tier) -> enterprise customers pinned to active-passive leader topology for reduced inconsistency exposure.
- route.failfast_on_leadership_loss -> control-plane client should fail-fast on a 503 + leadership-redirect to avoid inconsistent writes.

DR and evacuation runbook (concise steps for on-call):
1) Detection:
   - Alert on leader_epoch jumps > 1 without controlled deploy, repeated lease_renew_failures, or >3 regions reporting route_revocation_count spike.
2) Triage quick checks (first 10 minutes):
   - Query /leader/status across control-plane endpoints (use our diagnostic script cp-leader-check). Collect lease_acquired and leader_id.
   - Confirm network path status (BGP/Cloud inter-region) and load balancer health.
3) For suspected split-brain (two active leaders):
   - Immediately open paging to platform lead and SRE lead.
   - Evaluate affected customers (use live customer-impact dashboard).
   - If active-passive eligible: fence the lower-epoch leader via arbiter API (arbiter/fence?leader_id=).
   - If active-active: escalate to manual reconciliation; freeze writes for conflicting key spaces by toggling maintenance-mode for affected leader regions.
4) For full-region outage (regional control-plane unreachable):
   - Promote standby leader in fallback region using controlled failover script (cp-failover --promote regionB --grace 30s).
   - Verify promotion by reading leader_epoch and performing a canary write-read cycle for a synthetic customer.
5) Post-incident reconciliation:
   - Run state-delta tool (cp-diff) to produce list of divergent keys. Reapply with highest-revision wins policy or manual reconciliation for safety-critical entries.
   - Run pre-approved customer notifications and schedule per-customer verification for top 10 enterprise tenants.

Testing and rehearsal recommendations:
- Quarterly chaos tests that simulate asymmetric inter-region latency and one region full blackout. Record MTTR and false-positive leadership loss.
- Runbook dry-run during weekly on-call handoff for first-level engineers (walkthrough of the cp-leader-check and cp-failover scripts).
- Add canary customers that accept automated failover (non-critical traffic) to get real-world exercises.

Operational instrumentation (must-haves):
- Real-time map: region -> current_leader_id, leader_epoch, lease_ttl_remaining.
- Time-series: leadership_transitions per minute, leader_renew_fail_rate, fencing_actions_count.
- Distributed tracing tag: control.leader_id on control-plane API traces to correlate errors with leader changes.
- Automatic synthetic canary write every 15s per region (flagged as low-cost telemetry).

Implementation checklist (short actionable items):
- [ ] Implement lease-based leadership with observable metrics (team: controlplane-runtime).
- [ ] Build global arbiter service (3x instances across regions; infra ticket: JIRA-PLAT-4112).
- [ ] Add routing primitives and client-side failfast behavior to SDKs (devexp + controlplane teams).
- [ ] Create cp-leader-check, cp-failover, cp-diff scripts and add them to on-call playbooks.
- [ ] Add chaos test cases to the SRE repo with gating for releases.

Open questions / risks to surface:
- How to handle large-scale metadata churn if we adopt aggressive active-active for certain workloads? (risk: higher reconciliation complexity)
- Is our KMS/HSM integration safe during leader fencing? We must ensure keys cannot be double-used during split-brain.
- Operational cost: arbiter service adds maintenance burden—need run-level agreement.

Appendix: quick cheat commands (for on-call)
- cp-leader-check --all-regions -> prints leader_id, epoch, ttl_remaining
- cp-failover --promote regionX --confirm -> promotes standby leader after a grace period
- cp-diff --region-a R1 --region-b R2 > divergence.csv -> export for reconciliation

Notes to self / next steps:
- Share this draft with SRE and product security for feedback; incorporate KMS handling notes.
- Pair with UX team to make leadership redirects visible in control-plane client error messages.

End of document.
